published_prior_art.cite: TchetgenTchetgenVanderWeele2012 and RigdonHudgens2015 give finite intervals in distinct two-stage partial-interference designs.
CaiLow2004 and ArmstrongKolesar2018 supply Gaussian-modulus templates, not the stated compact nonidentical erasure posterior-spread result.

KandirosHarshawSavje2026 gives design-and-estimator minimax squared-risk bounds under arbitrary neighborhood interference, not an honest confidence-interval expected-length frontier for fixed unequal-clique Bernoulli assignment.
KandirosHarshawSavje2026 studies bias-variance tradeoffs and difficult-vertex removal for minimax squared risk; this finite trimming upper bound is a specialized but distinct confidence construction.
No checked comparator gives the displayed capped weighted-erasure confidence modulus, its finite water-filling certificate, and its trimmed-radius equivalence.
BasseAiroldi2018 gives nonconcentration limitations under interference, but not this boundary; the proposed result is chiefly a corollary of the water-filling frontier.

source_verification_receipts.version: PMC-hosted manuscript corresponding to the 2012 Statistical Methods in Medical Research article
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper constructs finite-sample Hoeffding-type confidence intervals for direct, indirect, total, and overall effects under two-stage group randomization, principally for binary outcomes.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Abstract; Sections 3--4 in the article page
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper studies binary-outcome partial-interference two-stage experiments and constructs exact confidence intervals by inversion of permutation-based tests under stratified interference.

source_verification_receipts.version: Author preprint corresponding to Annals of Applied Statistics 11 (2017)
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper supplies a design/exposure/estimand framework, inverse-probability estimators, conservative randomization variance estimators, and asymptotic intervals under local-dependence conditions.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Abstract; Introduction, paragraphs defining full-neighborhood exposure and variance behavior
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper defines treatment and control network exposure, uses inverse weighting, and shows exposure-probability-driven variance can grow exponentially with degree under unsuitable randomization.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Introduction; Sections 4 and E listed in the paper contents
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper develops conflict-graph-guided experimental designs, analyzes a modified Horvitz--Thompson estimator, and includes finite-sample variance, consistency, and inference analyses.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Abstract; Introduction pp. 1--4; informal main result and Corollaries 1.1--1.2
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper gives upper and lower design-based minimax squared-risk rate bounds over designs and estimators under arbitrary neighborhood interference, using a conflict graph, including DTE and GATE examples.
The paper develops nonasymptotic confidence intervals for ordinary randomized experiments with effective sample sizes matching asymptotic counterparts and information-theoretic rate lower bounds.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Turn the weighted-erasure posterior-spread OEQ into the first Stage-0 kill test: prove a two-prior interval-averaging inequality that explicitly retains external randomization, then state the largest admissible universal constants or a counterexample family.

Add a short formal comparison proposition specializing the 2026 conflict-graph squared-risk framework to unequal clique graphs and showing exactly why it neither implies nor is implied by uniform-coverage expected-length risk.

After the global water-filling equivalence is established, promote the consistency-boundary theorem to a stated corollary and add a triangular array where untrimmed S fails to vanish while the trimmed modulus vanishes.

recommended_next_step: Advance to Stage 0 with the weighted-erasure posterior-spread OEQ as the decisive solve target; retain the capped water-filling equivalence as the separate global extension.
